role: population/employment projection author (Erie and Niagara Counties Regional Planning Board)
stance_basis: cited as data source for population and employment projections without expressing support or opposition to the project
summary: ENCRPB (Erie and Niagara Counties Regional Planning Board) is cited throughout the document as a source of population and employment projections for the Buffalo SMSA, City of Buffalo, Amherst, and Tonawanda. The board's projections are used to characterize the regional economic and demographic context for the transit project, including forecasts of employment growth, labor force trends, and commuting patterns. ENCRPB does not express a position on the project itself; it functions solely as a data provider.
complaint_summary: ENCRPB is cited for labor force projections showing SMSA labor force growth of 2,750 annually while the City's labor force declines by 1,000 per year, implying increased suburban-to-city commuting and growing importance of transportation access.

statement.text: The size of the labor force (available potential workers) in the Buffalo SMSA is projected to increase an average of 2,750 annually between 1980 and 1995, according to the ENCRPB. The labor force residing within the City of Buffalo is projected to decline by 1000 persons annually between 1980 and 1995, whereas about half the increase in employment opportunities will be within the City. This means that there will be more workers commuting from suburban areas to the City for daily employment than at present, an increase of over 1100 from Amherst and over 2500 from other suburban portions of Erie County. Transportation access will become an increasingly important economic consideration.
statement.opening_anchor: The size of the labor force (available potential workers) in the Buffalo SMSA is projected to increase an average of 2,750 annually between 1980 and 1995, according to the ENCRPB.
statement.closing_anchor: Transportation access will become an increasingly important economic consideration.

summary_quote: Employment within the Buffalo SMSA is projected to increase an average of 2,550 to 2,800 annually between 1980 and 1995, according to the ENCRPB and the U.S. Department of Commerce.
